body:
Scope: renewed M1 milestone judgment after the user-requested public-skill portability correction on PR #175. This is a new assessment of the exact current M1 subjects; it does not retarget the prior final review or Verify. The complete implementation remains governed by the unchanged approved proposal, two-model Design and amended Delivery allocation.

Independently inspected the complete correction diff and both shared resources in full. The two introductions now express customer project policy/contract precedence, explicit adoption and preservation of historical meaning without internal RC requirement IDs or internal Design-checkout commentary. All fourteen skill-local copies match their canonical resources byte-for-byte. I directly checked that only the introduction paragraphs changed and the substantive rule bodies are identical to the previously assessed engineering contribution. Canonical search finds no RC-SR/RC-DEC/internal-Design references. Removal does not weaken policy ownership: customer authority explicitly remains authoritative, while internal traceability remains in the unchanged governing model and clause map. The three candidate archive hashes, current release-index digest and one matching package-test tree-hash pin are the expected generated consequences; no historical metadata entry or public runtime interface changes.

Checklist disposition: spec alignment, coverage, edge cases, error handling, architecture, compatibility, security/privacy, derived currency, unrelated-change scope and validation evidence all pass for this correction and renewed M1 claim. The public-facing concern is addressed without losing independence, judgment precedence, scope, finding ownership, bookkeeping/new-evidence handling, proof reuse, final whole-change checkpoint, distinct Verify or separately authorized external-action rules. No new material correction emerged.

Fresh evidence inspected in public-skill-portability-correction: python scripts/validate-skills.py (20); python scripts/build-skills.py --check; python scripts/test-skill-validator.py (370); targeted current-candidate adapter metadata test; all three current adapter archive generation/validation and Markdown scan; npm test --prefix packages/rigorloop (654 total, 652 passed, 2 skipped). I read the completed focused logs and independently checked local resource equality, unchanged substantive bodies and git diff --check.

Reuse assessment: prior passing lifecycle/selector/model/structural and historical-fixture proof remains applicable to its unchanged implementation, tests, governing inputs, dependencies and environment. The correction changes only customer-facing introductions and resulting archive metadata/test expectation, which now have fresh focused proof. Existing manual semantic scenarios remain valid for byte-identical rule bodies, while the changed introductions received independent semantic reassessment here. This is affirmative unaffected-surface reuse, not a claim that an earlier command ran on corrected bytes. Any expressly required fresh/current-state check still overrides ordinary reuse; current records and renewed final assessment/Verify remain separate obligations. Repeating unchanged full lifecycle snapshot traversal solely because this review is fresh is unnecessary.

M1 can return to route with this renewed milestone judgment. A distinct fresh final whole-change assessment after M1 closes is still required, followed by renewed Verify on applicable current evidence. Prior review/Verify identities and any immutable finding origins remain truthful. No hosted-CI result for the pending correction is claimed.
independence_basis: Separate delegated agent /root/independent_proposal_review performed this assessment. Root authored implementation and coordinated proof. This reviewer authored no engineering subjects, tests or packaged resources; earlier independent upstream reviews are assessment work, not engineering authorship. Independence is an actual separate execution, not an author role reset.
